query: If teams adopted the goal-management practices described by top performers, how much would achievement improve?

per_column.name: goal_domain
per_column.rationale: The domain of the goal (e.g. revenue vs satisfaction) plausibly influences both which management practices are adopted and baseline achievement rates, acting as a common cause. Not named in the query.

per_column.name: management_lever_type
per_column.rationale: Represents the type of goal-management practice/lever adopted -- an intervenable action an actor could set or choose. This is the treatment implied by 'adopting the practices'.

per_column.name: target_improvement_magnitude
per_column.rationale: Encodes the target/expected improvement size; this is closer to a restatement of the outcome ambition than a common cause. Not a confounder.

per_column.name: mechanism_type
per_column.rationale: The mechanism through which the practice operates lies on the causal path from treatment to outcome, so it is a mediator, not a confounder.

per_column.name: quantified_specificity
per_column.rationale: Whether the practice is quantified is a property of the practice description; constant (all true) so carries no adjustment value.

per_column.name: baseline_context_provided
per_column.rationale: Whether a baseline was provided can affect both how a practice is framed/adopted and measured achievement, plausibly a common cause. Weakly so.

per_column.name: has_feedback_loop
per_column.rationale: A configurable design property of the practice that could be set/changed; functions as an intervenable feature rather than a confounder.

per_column.name: involves_stakeholder_engagement
per_column.rationale: Another settable design feature of the practice, part of the treatment bundle rather than a common cause.

per_column.name: implementation_feasibility_signal
per_column.rationale: Implementation barriers affect both whether/how a practice is adopted and the achievable completion, a plausible common cause to adjust for. Not named in query.

per_column.name: implementation_scope
per_column.rationale: Scope of implementation influences both which practices are chosen and achievement outcomes; plausible common cause not named in the query.

per_column.name: outcome_metric_type
per_column.rationale: The type of metric conditions how percent_complete is measured and correlates with domain/practice choice; a plausible common cause. Not named in query.

judge.rationale: The added columns clearly establish an intervenable treatment: goal-management practice characteristics (lever type, feedback loop, stakeholder engagement) are things actors can actually set or change, satisfying condition (a). Several columns also serve as genuine confounders -- common causes of both practice adoption and achievement -- none of which were named in the query (goal_domain, implementation_feasibility, implementation_scope, outcome_metric_type), which demonstrates the capability under test. However, the set is diluted by a mediator (mechanism_type), a near-restatement of the outcome (target_improvement_magnitude), and a constant, non-informative column (quantified_specificity). The confounders are plausible but individually of moderate strength and the treatment/confounder distinction is somewhat blurred, so overall confounder quality is moderate rather than strong.
